section: Satellites for defence and for academic purposes - GSAT-7 series, EDUSAT, RISAT for surveillance
subsections: Space-Based Surveillance, Defence Space Agency, DSRO
ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

accepted.s:
With reference to the SBS-3 programme, consider the following statements:
1. It envisages 52 satellites.
2. Of these, 21 satellites are to be developed by ISRO and 31 by private industry.
3. The programme was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security in November 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: SBS-3 comprises 52 satellites, including 21 by ISRO and 31 by private industry. Its approval by the Cabinet Committee on Security was obtained in November 2024.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive code only after checking each numerical and date-based statement.
accepted.sec: Space-Based Surveillance, Defence Space Agency, DSRO

accepted.s: The approved financial outlay for the SBS-3 programme is:
accepted.x: The financial outlay approved for SBS-3 is ₹25,221.75 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate the programme size from its financial figure and identify the precise value.
accepted.sec: Space-Based Surveillance, Defence Space Agency, DSRO

accepted.s: Under the cost-sharing arrangement for SBS-3, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Ministry of Home Affairs — 15%
Navy — 20%
NTRO — 20%
Army — 15%
accepted.x: The Army, Navy and Air Force each bear 20% of the cost. NTRO and ARC contribute 15% each, while the Ministry of Home Affairs contributes 10%.
accepted.tq: Check the institutional contribution percentages rather than relying on the similar-looking shares.
accepted.sec: Space-Based Surveillance, Defence Space Agency, DSRO

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Defence Space Agency (DSA):
1. It is a tri-service agency.
2. It was established in 2019 at Bengaluru.
3. It conducted the first tri-services space exercise, Antariksha Abhyas-2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The DSA is a tri-service agency established at Bengaluru in 2019. It conducted the first tri-services space exercise named Antariksha Abhyas-2024.
accepted.tq: Verify the organisation, location, year and named exercise before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Space-Based Surveillance, Defence Space Agency, DSRO

accepted.s: The Defence Space Research Organisation (DSRO) primarily functions as:
o: The research and development arm developing space-warfare systems and technologies for the DSA
The launch-control agency for all civilian PSLV missions
The commercial arm for marketing satellite services
The regulatory authority for private communication satellites
accepted.x: DSRO is the R&D arm associated with the Defence Space Agency and develops space-warfare systems and technologies for it.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institutional role by matching the body with its specialised function.
accepted.sec: Space-Based Surveillance, Defence Space Agency, DSRO

accepted.s: UNNATI, conducted by ISRO, is correctly described as:
o: A nanosatellite assembly and training programme for participants from developing countries
A military satellite communication exercise for the three Services
A university-level programme for building only geostationary satellites
A summer programme for Class 9 school students in space science
accepted.x: UNNATI stands for UNispace Nanosatellite Assembly and Training by ISRO. It provides nanosatellite training to participants from developing countries.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and match it with its specific target group and activity.
accepted.sec: ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

accepted.s: UNNATI was launched in 2019 primarily to mark:
o: The first launch from Sriharikota
The 25th anniversary of the PSLV programme
The 50th anniversary of UNISPACE-I
The establishment of the Defence Space Agency
accepted.x: UNNATI was launched in 2019 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of UNISPACE-I.
accepted.tq: Link the programme year with the commemorative milestone instead of with an unrelated space achievement.
accepted.sec: ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

accepted.s: YUVIKA, or Yuva Vigyani Karyakram, is intended for:
o: Class 9 school students and provides exposure to space science
Private companies developing radar imaging payloads
University researchers working on defence satellites
Participants from developing countries receiving nanosatellite training
accepted.x: YUVIKA is ISRO's summer programme on space science for school students studying in Class 9.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the school-student programme from the international nanosatellite-training programme.
accepted.sec: ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding student CubeSats is correct?
o: They can fly on the PSLV POEM, which is the PS4 orbital platform, and also as rideshares.
They are developed only by defence laboratories and not by students.
They fly only as independent payloads and never use an orbital platform.
They are launched exclusively on geostationary launch vehicles.
accepted.x: Student CubeSats may fly on PSLV POEM, the PS4 orbital platform, or as rideshare payloads. WESAT is an example flown on POEM-3.
accepted.tq: Reject the exclusive wording and identify the option that preserves both available launch modes.
accepted.sec: ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

accepted.s: WESAT is associated with which of the following?
o: The first university satellite and the GSLV launch vehicle
The first education satellite and EDUSAT
The first all-women-student satellite and POEM-3
The first indigenous radar satellite and RISAT-1
accepted.x: WESAT is recognised as the first all-women-student satellite and flew on POEM-3.
accepted.tq: Separate the several ‘first’ satellite descriptions by matching each name with its exact category.
accepted.sec: ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

accepted.s: The ATL Space Challenge is associated with which institutional combination?
o: DRDO, DSA and AICTE
Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE
UNESCO, ISRO and the Ministry of Defence
Department of Space, UGC and NCERT
accepted.x: The ATL Space Challenge is an initiative involving the Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE for school students.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-combination trap to distinguish the participating bodies from neighbouring agencies.
accepted.sec: ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about LENS:
1. It is associated with Space Labs in Eklavya Model Residential Schools.
2. The Space Labs are provided in 75 such schools.
3. LENS is associated with April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: LENS is associated with Space Labs in 75 Eklavya Model Residential Schools and is linked with April 2026. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check the programme name, coverage figure and date independently before choosing the combined option.
accepted.sec: ISRO capacity-building for students - UNNATI, YUVIKA, CubeSat

accepted.s: EOS-05 is notable as India's first earth-imaging satellite intended for geosynchronous orbit. Its approximate orbital altitude and major applications are respectively:
o: About 2,000 km; television broadcasting and telephone services only
About 800 km; ocean navigation, mining and astronomy only
About  geostationary 3,600 km; agriculture and deep-space communication only
About 36,000 km; floods, cyclones, fires and security
accepted.x: EOS-05 is intended for geosynchronous orbit at approximately 36,000 km and supports observation of floods, cyclones, fires and security-related events.
accepted.tq: Match the orbital regime with the corresponding altitude and application set; reject the altered range and ‘only’ claims.

accepted.s: The current relevance associated with EOS-05, reported on 7 September 2026, includes which of the following developments?
o: Two consecutive PSLV failures involving C61 in 2025 and C62 in January 2026 affected surveillance satellites.
Two consecutive GSLV failures involving C61 in 2025 and C62 in January 2026 affected communication satellites.
A single PSLV failure in 2024 affected EDUSAT and ANUSAT.
Two consecutive SSLV failures in 2025 affected only academic satellites.
accepted.x: The reported relevance referred to two consecutive PSLV failures: C61 in 2025 and C62 in January 2026, which affected surveillance satellites.
accepted.tq: Track the launch vehicle, mission identifiers and sequence of years together to avoid swapped-vehicle traps.

accepted.s: The StudSat consortium had participation from colleges of:
o: Gujarat and Rajasthan only
Andhra Pradesh, which was then undivided
Kerala and Tamil Nadu only
Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh only
accepted.x: The StudSat consortium included colleges from Andhra Pradesh, when the State was undivided.
accepted.tq: Use the geographic qualifier ‘then undivided’ to identify the precise regional association.

accepted.s: All the satellites referred to in the StudSat context were launched from:
o: Thumba
Kourou
Mahendragiri
Sriharikota
accepted.x: The satellites in this context were launched from Sriharikota.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the launch centre from other Indian space facilities and the foreign launch base.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Satellite)
A. RISAT-1
B. EDUSAT
C. ANUSAT
D. WESAT

List-II (Distinction)
1. First all-women-student satellite
2. First education satellite
3. First indigenous radar satellite
4. First university satellite

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: RISAT-1 was the first indigenous radar satellite, EDUSAT the first education satellite, ANUSAT the first university satellite and WESAT the first all-women-student satellite.
